newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian bourse launches three indices.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian bourse launches three indices.

text.p: Lithuania's bourse launched three indices on Thursday three years after it started operations and officials were bullish on the market's future.
"We were reluctant to introduce indices earlier because of the small level of capitlisation and liquidity on the market," bourse director Rimantas Buslia told a news conference.
"The Lithuanian market has now reached a stage where the stock market has an important role to play."

The group A index will track 22 companies which comprise 32 percent of the market's capitalisation and whose shares have accounted for 63 percent of the central market's turnover since September of this year.
Group G contains the less active companies listed on the bourse while group VVP follows the secondary T-bill market.
Lithuania's bourse was rocked earlier this year by a banking crisis but seems to have recovered since.

Brokers say that a measure of confidence has been restored to the market. Central market volumes and the prices of leading shares have risen recently as investors have switched from debt to equity in response to lower T-bill yields.
The index for Group A has risen from 1,000 to 1,719.96 since the start of the year, the stock exchange said.
Group G has risen from 1,000 to 1302.17 in the same period while group VVP jumped from 1,000 to 1,205.07.
The group A index rose slightly on Thursday by 0.29 percent and central market volume reached almost 650,000 litas.
